comments.text: I’m a retired Social Worker and remember working with a family of five little girls youngest a baby oldest 8 ! You’d go in the house parents smothered in gold chains , house done out all lovely, it was a town house with three floors as you went  up you caught a whiff of urine , on middle floor , parents room with a 4 poster with all the trimmings- a room with a lock on the outside, when I asked them to open it after a bit of protesting and me threatening them with the police - it had brand new beds in the plastic , new bedding in the plastic toys in boxes , bikes brand new , Dollie’s in the boxes , dolls prams never used , it was like a shop !the top of the house was freezing 2 more bedrooms with locks, another room full to the brim of new clothes and toys - then the last room , where there was broken window, one filthy pillow on the floor and one single duvet that looked like it had been trampled in horse shit for 3 months and the stench of urine was eye watering- four children shared that tiny room, no carpet , no beds just floor boards and that filthy single duvet to keep them warm .The  previous social worker had got grants for clothing beds and bedding , toys for Christmas, the children never received them as this was in February! I went to see the eldest child at school who begged me not to talk to her as it made everything worse - we’d had a referral from the lady in the bakery in Sainsbury’s about this same child shaking with fear and crying because they didn’t have the exact bread rolls her mother had instructed her to buy . This woman followed this child through the checkout, she had a full trolly of food which she proceeded to push nearly two miles through one of the most dodgy places in that town - - she was doing the full shopping for her mother at just 8 years old and having to walk home in the dark with it . I was newly qualified at the time and remember literally begging on my hands and knees for an intervention and removing these kids to a place of safety but because the child herself was too terrified to say a thing to me I was told there was nothing they could do . It was only after speaking to a police officer because we did that back in those days did the Police do an early morning 6am welfare check to find the girls all locked in that stinking room , all malnourished - tied up upstairs until the 8 years old old came and took responsibility for the two youngest 2 &3 years - nappy rash like you’ve never seen it was traumatic! But they did eventually get removed and parents - well it’s the U.K. isn’t it ? Slap on the wrist for child neglect and abuse - last I heard she was still having babies ? There are just some really sadistic people in this world and after nearly 30 years of having to deal with that 5% I’m done burnt out because these people do not get sentenced, it’s as if it’s ok to do this again and again - they send them on a parenting course so they can disguise their abuse of their children more effectively! Just wish the public were fully aware that it’s never the decision of a single SW to remove children, the layers of management and layers of red tape you have have to go through is what enables this and in the past 15 years it’s got worse !

comments.text:
Thank you for covering this. They deserved to have their story told. 

My mother got away with several things comparable to what these kids went through. Religious Christian fundamentalist. Lots of death in my family. I didn’t understand medication or doctors surgery when I escaped. 

It was also the friends I made online, stealing WiFi, that told me it wasn’t normal either. The violence, abuse, beatings and starvation were things I never wanted any child to feel like I had to. I was 89lbs. At 18. I had been so severely starved that I developed numerous health complications. I would also sing and post it and make music.

My older brother took his own life because of our mother when I was a teen.

The biggest difference was  that my stepdad passed way in a violent car accident so, he wasn’t there.

But I was denied doctors, schooling, outside experiences, friends and basic needs like toothpaste.

It’s when she joined up a cult called the international house of prayer that things escalated out of control. Too many unspeakable things.

I know it’s not the same. But the feelings they had and must have had are relatable. It breaks my heart they went from one bad situation to another, but at least there’s justice. Maybe I’m living through this vicariously. 

My siblings didn’t get out. They always went back. It’s all they knew.

I’m okay now. Married to a lovely girl who helped me get out and acclimated me to the world. A found family that got me well. I eat when I’m hungry. I make music for a living and teach voice. I’m still physically ill and I will probably never improve. But I’m grateful. I hope the same for them. I hope they get to experience things that are good and they learn people are inherently kind. You just have to give them a chance to be. There’s a world to explore out there that isn’t full of the abuse and heartache no child should ever endure.

It means a lot when these stories get told. I feel a little less alone and more validated seeing how people react to this. Covering these stories matters. It makes a difference. 

Keep going. I really enjoy watching you tell stories.
